title: I built an AI app that analyzes trading chart screenshots. Here’s a real XAUUSD example 📊
author: xMavchartAI
selftext:
Hey everyone! 👋  
I’ve been working on an iOS app called **xMav Chart AI**, which analyzes trading chart screenshots using AI.  
The idea is simple: upload a chart and receive a structured analysis with potential BUY, SELL or WAIT setups, including entry zones, stop loss and take profit levels.  
Here’s a real example from XAUUSD on the M15 timeframe:  
🔴 Signal: SELL  
📊 Setup score: 90/100  
🎯 Entry zone: 4123.80–4124.40  
🛑 Stop loss: 4128.68  
✅ TP1: 4120.11  
✅ TP2: 4115.12  
✅ TP3: 4110.60  
The price later moved below the TP3 level, as shown in the TradingView screenshot.  
Of course, one example doesn’t prove long-term accuracy, and this isn’t a claim of an executed profitable trade.  
I’m currently looking for honest feedback from traders who use AI tools.  
**Would you use AI as a second opinion when analyzing charts? What would make a tool like this genuinely useful to you?**  
The app is now available on the App Store. 🚀

replies.author: jannieq
replies.body: Will appreciate if u can offer- shall be thankful

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: a 90/100 setup score doesn't tell anyone much until you've logged a few hundred of those calls and checked whether the 90s actually did better than the 60s. have you got that table yet?

replies.author: xMavchartAI
replies.body:
Great point! The 90/100 score represents the AI’s assessment of the setup quality, considering factors such as market trend and risk/reward. It’s not intended to represent a 90% win probability.  
The app is designed to provide structured chart analysis and a second opinion, not guaranteed trading outcomes.  
Comparing performance across score ranges is definitely something I want to expand on as more data becomes available. Appreciate the feedback! 📊

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: fair, as a setup grade that's fine. it still needs its own report card though: bucket the 90s and the 60s and see whether the 90s actually moved further your way. if they don't, it's a confidence number with nothing under it.
